similarity.method: L2-normalized title TF-IDF unigram/bigram channel centroid cosine
similarity.samplingNote: Purposive metadata sample; no population inference. Same video ID appears once. Distinct reposts can share underlying sessions.

limitations: Search and curated research samples are nonrandom and incomplete. No population prevalence or channel-wide posting rate is estimated.
Durations imported from the supplied Claude draft retain their unverified-provider provenance.
Missing duration and date values remain null; relative dates are not converted to exact dates.
Account routes are only merged using explicit aliases/IDs; unresolved aliases can split an account.
Distinct uploads can repeat the same original session. Video-ID deduplication does not establish recording-level independence.
Title vocabulary reflects publishers and upload packaging; it is not transcript content or evidence about the ontological source of channeling.

figures.title: Observed duration by channel
figures.caption: Each row uses available duration metadata for unique indexed video IDs. Labels show measured/indexed counts. Dots are medians; whiskers are the 25th–75th percentiles, not confidence intervals; diamonds are means. Only channels with at least five durations are plotted. These are convenience samples, often capped by source listings, not channel-wide averages.

figures.title: Duration coverage
figures.caption: Counts refer to the merged research index. The pale portion includes videos without usable duration metadata. Channel order reflects sample size, not popularity, activity or the size of the entire account.

figures.title: Title topic indicators
figures.caption: A cell is the fraction of eligible sampled titles matching at least one predefined English keyword in that topic. Topics overlap and are not validated semantic classes. This measures headline vocabulary, not the contents of a session; multilingual and short titles can be missed. The 20 largest eligible title samples are shown.

figures.title: Shared title vocabulary
figures.caption: Cosines compare equal-video-weight TF-IDF centroids after masking common channeling identity terms. Values are descriptive similarity scores, not probabilities or evidence of shared origins. Each account has at least five eligible titles. The 18 largest samples are plotted; exact matrices are exported.
